note: Only ofatumumab was tested alone in WM (phase 2, 59% response) on in-vitro CD20 lysis and monkey data from CLL; ublituximab's WM ex-vivo ADCC edge was never tested in WM patients, and veltuzumab has no WM data.
label: Waldenström (anti-CD20 depleters)

engagement.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy (first ofatumumab patient trials, ~2004); monkey studies dated only by the 2009 BLA review. Quote is OCR text ('CD20°' = CD20+).
engagement.judgement: Opening proxy year; the monkey studies are known only from the BLA review.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkeys dosed with ofatumumab (B-cell depletion and toxicology)
engagement.note: Ofatumumab binds only primate CD20; monkeys showed rapid depletion of CD20+ B cells from blood and lymph nodes.
engagement.quote: In cynomolgus monkeys, administration of ofatumumab resulted in rapid depletion of CD20° B-cells from circulation and lymph nodes.

engagement.magnitude_basis: depletion of circulating B cells, monkey (qualitative) vs CLL patients 85-93%
engagement.population: Refractory CLL patients (no WM B-cell depletion data found)
engagement.confidence_note: Read in the FDA review text. Human readout is in CLL, not WM; the WM trial (Furman 2017) reported IgM response and clearance, not B-cell counts.
engagement.judgement: Paired by me across two FDA review documents (pharmacology and clinical pharmacology). Depletion of the CD20-bearing cell scored proximal: it is the target cell's own loss, not occupancy. Engagement from CLL patients accepted because engagement admits any dosed humans. Retrodiction rule: engagement is a claim about the target; rituximab (anti-CD20 depleter) depleted B cells in patients from 1994-97 and ofatumumab's own CLL trial was public in 2007, both before the monkey data (Bleeker 2007, FDA 2009), so retro, not same.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus monkeys dosed with ofatumumab (B-cell depletion and toxicology)
engagement.note: Retrodiction: CLL patients' B cells fell 85-93%, as in monkeys, but rituximab had depleted human B cells years before the monkey data were public.
engagement.short: Human B cells fell as in monkeys
engagement.quote: The median decrease in circulating B cells in BFR patients was 93% (n=70) after the 8" infusion and 91% (n=41) after the 12" infusion.

dose.confidence_note: Read in the FDA review text. Furman 2017 states the 2000 mg WM regimen was chosen on CLL clinical activity and the 1000 mg group's safety.
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the monkey work stated no exposure or regimen target, and its tolerability margin is disputed (sponsor NOAEL 100 mg/kg = 3.5x clinical dose; FDA reviewer NOAEL 20 mg/kg = 0.7x, LOAEL for focal brain arteritis), so no stated margin is scored. The WM regimen came from CLL patients, not a model.
dose.model: Cynomolgus monkeys dosed with ofatumumab (B-cell depletion and toxicology)
dose.note: Monkey doses were 0.7- and 3.5-fold the 2000 mg clinical dose; reviewer set NOAEL at the low dose (brain arteritis at high dose).
dose.short: Monkey margin disputed; no dose target
dose.quote: The nonclinical doses of 20 and 100 mg/kg are nominally 0.7-fold and 3.5-fold, respectively, of the clinical dose (assuming a patient weight of 70 kg).
dose.reason: No model dose target; WM dose from CLL

dose.note: Xenograft: initial plasma 5 ug/mL, expected to saturate CD20, inhibited tumour; regrowth below half-saturation; 5-10 ug/mL proposed for sustained activity.
dose.quote: In a mouse xenograft model, a single dose, resulting in an initial plasma antibody concentration of 5 microg/ml, which was expected to result in full target saturation, effectively inhibited human B-cell tumour development.
dose.judgement: The exposure target (plasma 5-10 ug/mL maintaining CD20 saturation) is stated by the xenograft/monkey paper itself, so it is this track's dose prediction; no tolerability margin stated.
dose.model: SCID mice bearing CD20+ human B-cell tumour xenografts dosed with ofatumumab (tumour growth vs plasma concentration)

dose.note: WM patients on 1000-2000 mg had troughs of 23-181 ug/mL before dose 4, well above the xenograft's 5-10 ug/mL saturation target.
dose.quote: C trough prior to Dose 4, μg/mL 13 23·4 (5,252) 21 181 (252)
dose.confidence_note: PMC full text (PMC5484580) Table 5 read; quote is a table row. Ctrough first posted with registry results 2012-04-30 (NCT00811733); paper online Dec 2016.
dose.judgement: Judgement call: paired by me; the WM trial does not cite the xenograft target. Early troughs before dose 2 (3.0 and 8.0 ug/mL) sat near or below it, but from dose 3 on troughs exceeded it in both groups, so same.
dose.magnitude_basis: plasma ofatumumab trough vs 5-10 ug/mL saturation target
dose.model: SCID mice bearing CD20+ human B-cell tumour xenografts dosed with ofatumumab (tumour growth vs plasma concentration)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Quote is 34 words. The FDA review also cites SCID xenografts of CD20+ human tumours as proof of concept; no WM-derived cells were used.
efficacy.judgement: This is the system Furman 2017 cites as the rationale for testing ofatumumab in WM.
efficacy.model: In-vitro CDC/ADCC on CD20+ malignant B cells (lines, primary CLL)
efficacy.note: Ofatumumab (2F2) lysed rituximab-resistant CD20-low targets by complement, predicting improved clinical activity in B-cell lymphoma.
efficacy.quote: Thus, with increasing evidence that mAb therapeutic activity in vivo depends on complement activation, these new CD20 reagents with their slow off-rates and increased potency in CDC hold considerable promise for improved clinical activity.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: overall response rate (CR+PR+MR) vs in-vitro lysis; no quantitative prediction
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract plus PMC full text (PMC5484580) read. Year set by the registry results posting (2012-04-30) for NCT00811733; paper online Dec 2016. Earliest public date: ASH 2010 abstract 1795 (Blood 116:1795, 2010-11-19), read in full.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: the class prediction (CD20 lysis gives responses) held, so same, direction only. The stronger claim that higher CDC would beat rituximab was not tested head to head; 59% sits inside rituximab's 25-75% WM range. Paired by me; the trial paper cites the in-vitro data only as rationale. Rule 6: the interim ORR (43%, 14 pts) was public as ASH abstract 1795 on 2010-11-19, earlier than the 2012 registry posting. Retrodiction rule: Rituximab, the same target and action, had already produced responses in WM patients (Byrd 1999, Dimopoulos 2002), so this model post-dates the patient result: a retrodiction. NCT01536067 (ofatumumab with bortezomib, combination) was scored under the combination ruling but terminated with 3 enrolled and 0 analysed for ORR, so it changes no status and stays in patient_trials.

efficacy.note: Single-arm phase 2, primary endpoint ORR with no preset success bar: 43% interim (ASH 2010), 59% final; responses as predicted, but rituximab had already shown WM responses.
efficacy.quote: 19 (51%, 95% CI 34·4-68·1) of 37 patients achieved an overall response after cycle 1 and 22 (59%, 42·1-75·2) of 37 achieved an overall response after the redosing cycle

efficacy.judgement: Kept on its own track: patient-derived ex-vivo system, different member. Rule 6: online 2014-12-31 sets the year. Sawas 2017 enrolled FL, MZL, CLL/SLL, MCL and DLBCL, no WM, so not_measured.
efficacy.model: WM patient NK cells, ex-vivo ADCC against autologous WM B cells
efficacy.note: Ublituximab beat rituximab in ADCC by WM patients' own NK cells; no ublituximab trial enrolled WM patients.
efficacy.quote: Taken together, these data show that the efficacy of NK cells against B-cell clones is greater with ublituximab than with rituximab, allowing the NK phenotypic features observed in WM to be bypassed.
efficacy.reason: WM results of ublituximab trial unreported

safety.confidence_note: Opening year is a proxy (first patient trials ~2004).
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkeys dosed with ofatumumab (B-cell depletion and toxicology)
safety.note: Monkeys showed infections from B-cell depletion, infusion reactions after repeated dosing with IL-6 and complement rise, and haemolytic anaemia.
safety.quote: Ofatumumab-treated cynomolgus monkeys only exhibited signs of infusion reactions after repeated dosing; these events resolved without treatment.

safety.magnitude_basis: infections and infusion reactions, presence in monkeys vs WM patients
safety.population: Untreated or relapsed WM (phase 2 interim, n=15)
safety.confidence_note: ASH 2010 abstract read in full; Furman 2017 (registry 2012) confirms: infusion reactions the commonest grade 3-4 event (11%), infections 49%. FDA PharmR 2009 states monkey infections were consistent with clinical observations (CLL) and humans were more sensitive to infusion reactions.
safety.judgement: Imported-harm ruling: WM patients were measured, so their result, not the CLL comparison FDA made, sets the status; paired by me (the abstract does not cite the monkey data). Retrodiction rule (safety: same drug only): ofatumumab's own CLL infections and infusion reactions were public 2007-11-14 (Coiffier 2008), before the monkey toxicology was public (FDA review 2009), so retro, not same. Partial because monkeys showed infusion reactions only after repeated dosing. One WM patient had grade 3 haemolytic anaemia (monkeys also showed it; FDA called it species-specific); brain arteritis at 3.5x the clinical dose is not scored.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkeys dosed with ofatumumab (B-cell depletion and toxicology)
safety.note: WM patients had infusion reactions and infections, as monkeys did, but reactions came at first dose; retro, since ofatumumab's CLL harms were public before the monkey data.
safety.quote: Infusion-related events occurred with dose 1 (300 mg) in 12 pts and with dose 2 (1000 mg) in 7 pts; all infusion events were grade 1–2 except 2 grade 3 events (rash, serum sickness).
